guideTitle: 6 Best Stainless Steel Divided Plates in 2026
metaDescription: Six stainless steel divided plates for adults compared by size, section depth, steel grade and set size, plus why metal never goes in a microwave.
introParagraphs: Stainless steel divided plates are the unbreakable, no-stain, no-odor option. They survive drops, picnics and years of dishwasher cycles, and they never absorb sauce the way plastic can. The catch is the one everyone should know up front: metal does not go in the microwave, so these are plates for eating from, not for reheating on.

Many listings are written for kids, and several lineup names say so, but the sizes tell the real story. The picks below run from an 8.1 inch round plate to a rectangular 11.2 by 8.7 inch tray with five sections. Steel grade, section depth and rim finish matter for adults. We evaluated each pick on those points, based on product specs and buyer feedback.

We did not rank anything on health claims. These are durable everyday plates, and the portion layouts are visual guides only. Read the picks, then use the choosing tables to match size, sections and set count to your kitchen.

products.name: DEAYOU 18/10 Stainless Steel Divided Plates, 4 Pack
products.description:
DEAYOU is the best balance of size, depth and steel quality. Each of the four plates measures about 10.2 by 7.4 inches and is 1.6 inches deep, with a four-section layout of one main and three sides. The listing specifies 18/10 (304) food-grade stainless steel that is extra thick and rust resistant. The depth is enough to hold soup or sauce without spilling easily.

The tradeoff is that it is branded as a small child plate in the title, so it can read as a kid product on the table. At 7.4 inches wide it is also narrower than a round dinner plate, so very large pieces of food will not lie flat. The four-section layout is flexible but the sections are small. Like all stainless, it cannot go in the microwave.

Ownership is easy, because the plates are dishwasher safe and smooth-edged, and stack for storage. Compared with the Offiper at 3 sections and 1.57 inches deep it offers a fourth section, and compared with the AIYoo at 11.2 by 8.7 inches it is smaller but in a set of four rather than two. It is the best-rounded pick for most kitchens.
products.bestFor: Everyday meals with a main and three sides.
pros: 18/10 (304) steel is thick and rust resistant
1.6 inches deep holds sauces and soups
cons: Title and look read as a kid plate

products.name: AIYoo Stainless Steel Divided Tray Plates, Set of 2
products.description:
AIYoo is the largest plate in the group at 11.2 by 8.7 inches, still 1.6 inches deep. It has five sections, two for mains and three for sides, which suits a full dinner with several components. The listing calls it 304 stainless steel and says it is a bigger size built for adults, and it ships as a set of two.

Five sections can be too many for plain meals. Each section is smaller than the equivalent on a three-section plate, and a single large food like a steak will not fit flat. The set of two is also the smallest buying unit, so a household needs more than one set. The plates are rectangular, so they take up rack space.

The larger size and extra sections give variety for people who like to keep many foods separate. Compared with the DEAYOU at 10.2 by 7.4 inches it is bigger and has one more section but fewer plates. Compared with the Offiper at three deep sections, it trades depth per section for variety. Pick it if you enjoy many small items on one tray.
products.bestFor: Adults who eat many small items per meal.
pros: 11.2 by 8.7 inches is the largest here
cons: Small sections cannot hold large foods

products.name: Offiper 304 Stainless Steel Compartment Plates, Set of 2
products.description:
Offiper is the pick for foods that are wet. The three sections are 1.57 inches deep, or 4 centimeters, and the listing contrasts them with shallow trays for holding soups, sauces, yogurt and curries. The steel is 304 (18/8), thick and sturdy, with smooth rolled edges that the maker says are comfortable to hold when washing.

With only three sections it is less versatile than the five-section AIYoo, and sections are larger than on the DEAYOU. It ships in a set of two, so a couple has one tray each and a family needs more. The listing says to wash before first use and that the trays are fully dishwasher safe. As with all stainless, it cannot be microwaved.

The deeper wells mean you can pour a sauce over rice without it creeping into the vegetables. Compared with the DEAYOU at 1.6 inches deep it is similar in depth but has fewer, larger sections. Compared with the WG at 1 inch deep it holds much more liquid. It suits cooks who eat curries, stews and bowls.
pros: Three larger sections hold full portions
Fully dishwasher safe per the listing
cons: Only two trays in the set

products.name: Bakpoco Stainless Steel 9 Inch Divided Plates, 4 Pack
products.description:
Bakpoco is the only round plate in the group at a true 9 inches. It has three sections laid out in a 2:1:1 ratio, one large and two smaller, which the listing links to protein, carbohydrates and fats. The material is 304 food-grade stainless steel and the plates are described as unbreakable and dishwasher friendly, in a set of four.

The round shape stacks tighter than the rectangles and looks closest to a conventional plate. The tradeoff is capacity, because 9 inches is limited for a big dinner, and the listing does not give a depth. The branding speaks to kids, but the diameter and ratio suit adults who want portion guidance. Metal cannot go in a microwave.

It is easy to live with, with a smooth surface that rinses clean and light handling. Compared with the PandaEar at 8.1 inches it is a full inch larger and has one extra plate, and compared with the DEAYOU at 10.2 by 7.4 inches it is rounder with fewer sections. It is the one to buy when you want something that looks like an ordinary plate.
products.bestFor: A conventional round look in stainless.
pros: 9 inch round looks like normal dinnerware
304 steel is unbreakable and stain free
cons: Depth is not stated on the listing

products.name: WG Stainless Steel 3 Section Divided Trays, 4 Pack
products.description:
WG offers a 10 by 10 inch square tray with three sections that is 1 inch deep, sold in a set of four. The listing gives the weight as 11.6 ounces per plate and says they are heavier duty than paper-thin steel plates. It adds that the dishes can be heated in the oven and are sticker free, which is a small but real convenience.

The 1 inch depth is shallow compared with the Offiper and DEAYOU, so soups and sauces will overflow. The listing also does not state the steel grade, so it is the least documented material here. The square plate has plenty of surface for dry foods, fruit, cookies and nuts. As with every stainless option, it cannot go in a microwave.

Ownership is simple, because the plates stack and the mirror polish wipes clean. Compared with the Bakpoco at 9 inches it is wider but shallower, and compared with the Offiper at 1.57 inches deep it holds far less liquid. It suits dry meals and oven warming.
pros: 10 by 10 inches gives wide dry-food room
Can be heated in the oven per the listing

products.name: PandaEar Stainless Steel 8.1 Inch Divided Plates, 3 Pack
products.description:
PandaEar is the smallest and lightest pick, a polished 8.1 inch round plate with three sections in a set of three. The listing says the steel is 100 percent food-grade 304, BPA-free and odor resistant, and that the surface is smooth enough to prevent residue buildup. It is stackable and dishwasher safe.

At 8.1 inches it is a small plate, closer to a snack or lunch plate than a dinner. The listing gives no depth, and the marketing is aimed at kids, so adult buyers should treat it as a compact portion plate. Only three plates ship per set, and like every plate here it is not for the microwave.

It is easy to handle because it is light and stacks flat. Compared with the Bakpoco at 9 inches it is smaller and has one fewer plate, and compared with the WG at 10 by 10 inches it holds much less. It is a good fit for lunches, snacks and travel.
pros: 8.1 inch round is light and compact
cons: Too small for a full dinner

buyingCriteria.explanation: Metal plates cannot go in the microwave, and that is the single biggest tradeoff versus plastic or ceramic. Every pick here, from the DEAYOU to the PandaEar, is for eating from rather than reheating on. Plan to warm food in a microwave-safe dish, then plate it. The WG listing says its trays can be heated in the oven, which is a different use. If you reheat on the plate daily, choose ceramic or wheat straw instead.

Look for 304 stainless, sometimes written as 18/8 or 18/10, because it resists rust and does not flavor food. The DEAYOU lists 18/10 (304) and extra thick steel, the Offiper and Bakpoco list 304, and the AIYoo and PandaEar list 304 too. The WG does not state a grade, which makes it the least documented. Thicker steel feels sturdier and resists denting, so the WG at 11.6 ounces per plate is a useful clue.

Section depth separates plates for dry food from plates for wet food. The Offiper at 1.57 inches, the DEAYOU at 1.6 inches and the AIYoo at 1.6 inches hold sauces and soups, while the WG at 1 inch is for dry items. The Bakpoco and PandaEar do not publish depth. For curries, stews and yogurt, look for 1.5 inches or more. For sandwiches and fruit, 1 inch is enough.

More sections mean more separation but smaller wells. The AIYoo has five, the DEAYOU has four, and the Offiper, Bakpoco, WG and PandaEar have three. Five works for a varied tray, three works for a main and two sides. The Bakpoco uses a 2:1:1 ratio with one large section. If you eat large single items like chicken breast, choose fewer sections.

Rectangles hold more but need rack space, and rounds look more like ordinary plates. The AIYoo at 11.2 by 8.7 inches is the largest, the WG at 10 by 10 inches is wide, and the DEAYOU at 10.2 by 7.4 inches is narrower. The Bakpoco at 9 inches and PandaEar at 8.1 inches are round. Match the shape to your cabinet and dishwasher rack.

Stainless conducts heat, so a plate of hot food can be warm to hold. Smooth rolled edges, like the Offiper's, are safer for hands. The plates are light compared with ceramic, which helps weak wrists, but they slide on a smooth table. Use a damp cloth or mat under any steel plate to keep it from sliding. Check for rolled edges before buying a set.

howWeEvaluated.title: Steel grade and build
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at stated steel grades and thickness. The DEAYOU lists 18/10 (304) and extra thick steel, the Offiper, Bakpoco, AIYoo and PandaEar list 304, and the WG lists no grade but gives an 11.6 ounce weight. Documented grades ranked higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Section depth and layout
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared published depth and section counts. The Offiper at 1.57 inches and the DEAYOU and AIYoo at 1.6 inches lead for liquids, the WG at 1 inch is shallowest, and the Bakpoco and PandaEar publish no depth. Layout ranged from three to five sections.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size for adults
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared diameters and tray dimensions against adult meals. The AIYoo at 11.2 by 8.7 inches is the largest, the WG at 10 by 10 inches and DEAYOU at 10.2 by 7.4 inches follow, and the Bakpoco at 9 inches and PandaEar at 8.1 inches are the smallest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat and care limits
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each listing for care notes. Every plate is stainless and is not microwave safe, and the WG adds oven heating. The Offiper, DEAYOU and PandaEar state dishwasher safety. Plates without clear care instructions ranked lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Set size and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared what each set provides. The DEAYOU, Bakpoco and WG ship four plates, the PandaEar ships three, and the AIYoo and Offiper ship two. Larger sets ranked higher for households.

faq.q: Can stainless steel divided plates go in the microwave?
faq.a: No. Metal should never go in a microwave, and every plate here is stainless. Reheat food in a microwave-safe dish, then plate it. The WG listing does say its trays can be heated in the oven.

faq.q: Which stainless divided plate is best overall?
faq.a: The DEAYOU 4 Pack is the best all-rounder. It has thick 18/10 steel, a 1.6 inch depth and four plates. Choose the Offiper for soups, the AIYoo for big appetites, or the Bakpoco for a round look.

It is a common food-grade stainless steel that resists rust. The 18/8 and 18/10 labels refer to chromium and nickel content, with 304 being the usual grade. The DEAYOU lists 18/10 (304), and the Offiper, Bakpoco, AIYoo and PandaEar list 304.

faq.q: Are kids stainless plates fine for adults?
faq.a: Yes, if the size fits. The DEAYOU at 10.2 by 7.4 inches, AIYoo at 11.2 by 8.7 inches and WG at 10 by 10 inches are adult scale. The PandaEar at 8.1 inches is a snack size, so check diameters first.

faq.q: Do stainless plates get hot with food?
faq.a: Steel conducts heat, so a plate of hot food can feel hot to hold. Rolled edges like the Offiper's help. Let very hot food cool a moment, and use a mat under the plate.

faq.q: Will stainless plates rust or stain?
faq.a: Good 304 steel resists rust and does not hold odors. Avoid leaving salty food sitting for days and dry plates after washing. Pitting or rust spots usually mean a lower grade of steel.

faq.q: Why do my steel plates slide on the table?
faq.a: Steel plates are light and smooth underneath. A damp cloth or silicone mat stops most sliding. None of these picks has a suction base, so add a mat if stability is a concern.
